Electromagnetic wave absorbing materials (EWAMs) reduce radar detection by absorbing incident electromagnetic energy but are limited by coating thickness, incident angles, and frequency bands.
Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) consist of many low-cost passive elements that can independently adjust amplitude and phase of incident signals.
The proposed IRS-aided ES system deploys IRS on the target surface alongside EWAM to destructively combine reflected signals and reduce radar echo.
The received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the radar is minimized by optimizing IRS reflection coefficients under modulus constraints.
The optimization problem is convex and solved using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions to obtain a semi-closed-form solution.
Simulation results show that increasing the number of IRS elements significantly decreases the received SNR at the radar.
The IRS-aided system can achieve perfect stealth (SNR=0) when the number of IRS elements exceeds a threshold (e.g., N≥20).
Random phase shift IRS designs perform worse than the proposed optimized IRS reflection design.
The system model assumes a monostatic radar with uniform planar arrays (UPA) and far-field line-of-sight (LoS) channels.
The detection probability of the radar monotonically increases with received SNR, so minimizing SNR reduces detection probability.
The IRS reflection coefficient for each element is represented as θ[n] = β[n] e^{jφ[n]} with β[n] ∈ [0,1] and φ[n] ∈ [0,2π).
The EWAM absorption efficiency p is modeled in simulations ranging from 0 to 1 to evaluate performance impact.
The proposed IRS-aided ES system outperforms baseline schemes without IRS and with random IRS phase shifts in all tested scenarios.
The dual semidefinite programming problem for IRS design has computational complexity on the order of O(N^{4.5}).
The IRS requires no active RF chains, reducing deployment cost and energy consumption compared to active stealth technologies.
The solution leverages channel reciprocity and assumes channel coherence during optimization intervals.
The system uses a cross-shaped sensing array embedded at the ES surface center for angle-of-arrival estimation.
The proposed method is validated through extensive simulations with randomly generated AoA/AoD angles within ±π.
The IRS reflection coefficients can be precomputed offline and stored for real-time adaptation based on sensed angles.
The paper demonstrates the feasibility of combining IRS with EWAM for dynamic electromagnetic stealth in fast-changing radar environments.
